description:
## Goal

Make large immutable product values shared across producers, the memo, typed consumers, World projections, and cache hits without changing product keys, equality, generations, or dependencies.

## Evidence

On 00420 there are 206 each of Materialized, ABI, and Backend executable products. Current settle and typed-record paths perform at least 1,854 bookkeeping deep-clone passes, and Materialized-to-ABI, ABI-to-Backend, and Backend-to-root add at least 618 consumer-stage deep clones. Whole root programs are also cloned across World and memo settlement. The canonical backend dump is 1,479,209 bytes, demonstrating payload scale.

## Strategy and proof

1. Add a temporary clone/allocation counter around the large immutable payload boundaries.
2. Use one shared immutable handle for large `ProductValue` variants and `BackendProgram` / `NativeProgram` storage. Share group dependency maps where all members have the same dependencies.
3. Return shared values on cache hits; do not reconstruct owned trees merely to observe them.
4. Make large payloads non-`Clone` where practical so reintroduction fails to compile.
5. Preserve structural value equality as the generation-change rule and preserve ownership/dependency identity in `ProductKey`.
6. Prove identical product settlement counts, generations, causal traces, canonical artifacts, and runtime output, while the temporary counter shows no deep clone on settle or cache hit; then delete the counter.
7. Run full tests and strict clippy.

This is a representation change, not cache-key deduplication.
title: Share immutable product payloads instead of deep-cloning artifacts
